brief: A seven-cell honeycomb work surface, covered on top, with every open outside edge finished with caps.

requirements.evidence: Seven full hex bases on level 0: centre (0,0) plus the six neighbours (1,0), (1,-1), (0,-1), (-1,0), (-1,1), (0,1). Locked with six joint bolts on the centre-to-ring joints; check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear.
Seven top-face covers (cover:*;full;top), one on every cell including the centre.

requirements.requirement: Every open outside edge finished with caps
requirements.evidence: 18 caps (addCap, face *) on the six ring cells, three bearings each (150/210/90 etc.), which is every outside edge not shared with a neighbouring cell. Caps are the only items on the outer perimeter.

finish.summary: Built a seven-cell hex flower on one level, with top covers on all seven cells and 18 caps closing all outer edges. Added six joint bolts (not requested) to clear the loose-body warning. Final check: no rule issues, meshClash clear. The underside is open by design, since the brief only asked for top covering.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
